highest_risk_component.rationale: Component 'Appointment Search & Query Path' is determined as highest-risk because it contains 1 confirmed CRITICAL severity finding (SECURITY-001); exposes an unauthenticated CWE-89 SQL injection vulnerability; endpoint has 0% regression test coverage (TESTGAP-006); involves 4 HIGH severity findings.

Lines 74–77 contain the injection. Line 74 captures unsanitized user input: `status = request.args.get("status", "")`. Line 76 builds the SQL string by direct concatenation: `query = "SELECT * FROM appointments WHERE status = '" + status + "'"`. Line 77 executes the constructed query verbatim: `rows = db.execute(query).fetchall()`. There is no parameterization, allow-list validation, or escaping anywhere in this code path.

Requirement R004 mandates that all database queries use parameterized statements (prepared statements / bind variables) to prevent SQL injection. The search_appointments implementation directly violates R004 by constructing a query via string concatenation instead. Every other query in the codebase (appointment_service.py, notification_service.py, and the other endpoints in routes/appointments.py) correctly uses the `?` placeholder pattern required by R004; this endpoint is the sole non-compliant outlier introduced in the current diff.
Guard checks only 'completed'. The value 'cancelled' is absent from this condition. Execution continues to the INSERT INTO notifications statement at lines 32-35 for any cancelled appointment.

The dict literal contains seven keys: appointment_id, patient_id, doctor_id, appointment_date, status, priority, created_at. The key 'eta_minutes' is absent. All three endpoints (POST /appointments, GET /appointments/<id>, POST /appointments/<id>/cancel) serialise responses via this function, so all three violate R002.

                     CHECK (priority IN ('normal', 'high', 'emergency', 'critical')), | The migration file contains no CHECK constraint on priority and no 'critical' value. The application SCHEMA adds both the CHECK constraint and 'critical' without a corresponding versioned migration. R003 requires values 'normal', 'high', 'emergency' only; 'critical' is an unapproved addition. The migrations/ directory contains only 001_initial_schema.sql — no migration covering this change exists.

Line 76 concatenates user-supplied input (request.args.get('status')) directly into the SQL query string using string concatenation (+). No parameterized placeholder (?) is used. The function docstring at lines 69-72 explicitly notes: 'R004 violation: user-supplied status is concatenated directly into the SQL query string instead of using a parameterized placeholder.'

test_notifications.py contains four tests: test_reminder_sent_for_scheduled_appointment, test_reminder_response_contains_message, test_reminder_for_nonexistent_appointment, test_multiple_reminders_for_scheduled_appointment. The required test 'test_cancelled_appointment_does_not_trigger_reminder' is entirely absent.

test_appointments.py contains tests for creation, retrieval, and cancellation flows. The required test 'test_create_appointment_response_includes_required_fields' (R002) is absent — no test asserts the presence of 'eta_minutes' in any response. No test matching 'test_appointment_priority_persisted_*' (R003) is present — no test verifies that the priority value submitted at creation is retrievable via GET.

demo_target/db.py SCHEMA defines priority column with CHECK constraint and 'critical' value (line 49); migrations/001_initial_schema.sql defines the same column as `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'` with no constraint (line 26). The two definitions are out of sync and no migration bridges the gap.

migrations/ directory contains only 001_initial_schema.sql — no 002_* migration file exists to introduce the CHECK constraint or the 'critical' value into databases that were initialised incrementally from migration 001.

demo_target/models.py VALID_PRIORITIES (line 41) includes 'critical' — the application accepts and will attempt to persist a value not present in any migration, producing divergent validation behavior depending on which schema path was used to initialise the database.
